Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, dense opacity in the right upper hemithorax with ill-defined inferior margins, which is consistent with the heterogeneous appearance often caused by necrosis or hemorrhage in large pleuropulmonary synovial sarcomas. This aligns better than the description of a sharply marginated, uniform mass (Option B), as the lesion's borders are not clearly circumscribed on the radiograph.
